GenAI Basics • Lesson 14 • Rapid prototype03 / 17
Code (reference)

The whole chat is 14 lines: show history, take the question, ask the model, show the answer

app.py · run: streamlit run app.py
import streamlit as st

def ask_llm(messages):  # stub — replace with your L03 API call
    return "Demo answer: " + messages[-1]["content"]

st.title("Support assistant")

if "messages" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.messages = []          # chat memory

for m in st.session_state.messages:          # show history
    st.chat_message(m["role"]).write(m["content"])

if prompt := st.chat_input("Your question"):
    st.session_state.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": prompt})
    st.chat_message("user").write(prompt)
    answer = ask_llm(st.session_state.messages)   # ask the model
    st.session_state.messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": answer})
    st.chat_message("assistant").write(answer)
session_state — chat memory between clicks
for … chat_message — show the whole history
chat_input — the input box at the bottom
ask_llm — a stub for now; the agent swaps in a model call: Gemini, OpenAI, the local one from L10

How it works

On every click Streamlit reruns the whole file — that is why memory is needed

1
You click
or type
2
File reruns
top to bottom
3
Memory
session_state
4
Page
redrawn
app.py
Anything not stored in session_state disappears on the next click.
The most common beginner “bug” — “the chat gets wiped” — is not a bug, it is this loop.
GenAI Basics • Lesson 14 • Rapid prototype05 / 17
Three words

Memory, cache and secrets — three things not to mix up

session_state
one visitor’s memory: chat history, chosen settings
cache_data
a shared cache for everyone: faq.md is read once, not on every click
secrets
API keys in .streamlit/secrets.toml, never in code
A key in code = a key on GitHub (the site where code is stored) = a key for everyone. Add secrets.toml to .gitignore — the list of files that never go to GitHub.
GenAI Basics • Lesson 14 • Rapid prototype06 / 17
With an agent

A coding agent writes the code; you set the task and check the result

Prompt for a coding agent: Codex in ChatGPT or Antigravity (free, with limits), Claude Code (paid)
Build a Streamlit prototype: a chat assistant that answers staff from faq.md.
1. Python 3.11+, a separate environment:
   pip install streamlit google-genai
2. First run streamlit skills to add Streamlit’s official skills.
3. Model Gemini 3.8 Flash, key from st.secrets; with no key, a demo mode with a canned answer.
4. History in session_state, read faq.md with st.cache_data.
5. secrets.toml in .gitignore, plus a secrets.example.toml with a placeholder.
6. Run streamlit run app.py and explain every part of the code to me.
streamlit skills — an official command: it gives the agent instructions on writing Streamlit properly (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor).
A demo mode without a key — the prototype can be shown at once, even without paying for an API.
The last step is a must: ask the agent to explain the code.

Changed text or code — saved — clicked Rerun (the button appears top right). Handy to edit together with a client.

Publishing

Where to show a prototype: your computer, the free Streamlit cloud or your company cloud

Your own computer
free; you, and colleagues on the office network; share your screen to show
Streamlit Community Cloud
free, from a GitHub repo (a code folder); from a public repo it is public; only one private app
Your company
Snowflake (Streamlit’s owner), your own cloud — role-based access; engineers decide
A public link = public data and your API bill. Anyone with the link spends your quota. A public prototype gets synthetic data only.
A free app goes to sleep after 12 hours without visitors.

Security

Four prototype rules: keys, data, money, sign-in

Keys
only in secrets, not in code and not in the chat with the agent
Data
a public prototype — synthetic data only
Money
a spending limit in the API console; a demo mode with no key
Sign-in
a private Community Cloud app + email invites
A prototype is not a product. Until engineers and security review it, it does not touch real customer data.
